arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that a presumption of harm lacks support in precedent.
The government argues that the Guidelines remain central to federal sentencing.
Justice Alito questioned the allocation of the burden of persuasion in specific scenarios.
Justice Sotomayor challenged the distinction between general and specific evidence.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks if a court error in calculating sentencing guidelines automatically invalidates a sentence. the side that brought the case argues the error is not automatically harmful. The government argues the error is presumptively harmful.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on January 12, 2016.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to reject the presumption that guideline errors are always harmful.
The government wants the Court to treat guideline errors as automatically prejudicial.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that plain error review does not support a presumption of harm.
The government argues that the Guidelines are central to federal sentencing.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Alito asked if the burden of persuasion shifts to the prosecution when evidence is absent.
Justice Sotomayor asked why the side that brought the case labels certain evidence as general rather than specific.
